errors.quote: The chunk is only a tiny power $K=p^{\epsilon c}$ of $p$
errors.problem: Stated as an equality, but the paper sets $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ with $d=\lfloor b^\epsilon\rfloor$, $p=6b$, and only has $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ (eq. sizes, line 4070). The page itself wrote $K=\lfloor d^{c}\rfloor$ and $d=\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ a paragraph earlier. The exponent of the margin is unaffected.

errors.quote: The terms also carry fixed powers of $\log p$, for example the $O(p\log p)$ cost of multiplying two $p$-bit numbers, a normalized factor $\log p$. Half the margin pays for them
errors.problem: The example is in the wrong place. In the paper the $O(p\log p)$-per-entry products by $S$ are a separate additive cost, normalized to $O(\log p)=O(p^\delta)$ and listed in their own row of Table tab:costs ('Final scaling and rounding ... absorbed above', lines 4899-4900, 4829). They are not a $\log p$ factor on a dominant power $p^{1-2\kappa}$, and they do not need the $p^\kappa$ slack. The paper only says the slack 'will cover any remaining fixed power of $\log p$' (lines 4854-4855, 4984). The final bound is unaffected.
